A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConCon study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with neural and neuro-symbolic models on ConCon, including joint and continual training, learning curves, and class-specific error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional continual-learning comparisons in Tables 1 and 4 and appendix figures.

M1.justification: The ConCon generation rules, ResNet-18 architecture, and neuro-symbolic model procedure remain unchanged. Additional evaluated algorithms expand the comparison suite rather than introduce a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same disjoint and strict ConCon variants, three confounded tasks, and universal unconfounded dataset. The ground-truth rule, blue/metal/large confounders, visual domain, and 63,000-image collection are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds FROMP, DER, BGS, and GDUMB to the corresponding NN and NeSy comparisons on both ConCon variants. v1 evaluates only naive sequential training, EWC, ER, cumulative training, and joint training.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce method-specific buffer selection and a 30-epoch NN training budget for FROMP, documented in v2 Appendix B. Existing experiments retain their splits, accuracy metrics, 100-example ER buffer, and 50/150-epoch NN/NeSy budgets.

E4.justification: Appendix C extends the existing positive/negative error decomposition to the added methods, examining GDUMB's atypical failures and FROMP's class-performance tradeoffs. The cumulative-training convergence analysis and its learning curves are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides joint-training standard deviations and selected numerical or qualitative summaries of continual-training variability. v2 Table 4 systematically supplies per-result standard deviations across the comparison suite, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. Both versions specify five random seeds; no increase in repetitions is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for four comparison methods, including strict unconfounded accuracies of 49.5% for NN and 51.3% for NeSy with BGS. Retained mean accuracies match up to rounding. Some existing uncertainty values change: strict joint NeSy unconfounded accuracy has a standard deviation of 0.04 in v1 Table 2 versus 0.33 in v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same predicate definitions, strict/disjoint constraints, joint-solution derivations, and conditions making the ground-truth rule unique. Equations are consolidated and renumbered without a substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract slightly broadens the joint-versus-sequential claim from applying to 'many such continual datasets' in v1 to 'in general' in v2. The principal contributions and conclusions about ConCon, forgetting, and insidious continual confounding remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking GDUMB variability to buffer sampling and FROMP instability to decision-boundary sample selection. Appendix D explicitly discusses real-world and nonvisual applicability limits, extending restrictions already described in v1 Appendix A.2. The existing overfitting interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents PyTorch, EPYC CPU and Tesla V100 hardware, and training time below one hour per task. It also specifies a Croissant metadata record, the MIT code license, and PNG/class-separated data organization. These expand disclosure; dataset hosting and the BSD dataset license already appear in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the newly evaluated methods, Croissant metadata, and causal fairness. The related-work discussion and ConCon's positioning relative to confounded datasets and continual CLEVR remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, merges contribution bullets, revises the experimental narrative around the expanded comparisons, and adds a limitations appendix. Language is polished throughout, but most explanations and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v1's main accuracy heatmaps and separate joint-training tables are replaced by consolidated v2 Table 1, with a new uncertainty Table 4. Appendix heatmaps are reorganized around the expanded methods, and Figure 2's schematic is rearranged horizontally.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing study through more relevant comparisons, particularly BGS's treatment of spurious correlations, and makes uncertainty easier to assess through Table 4. Added implementation and applicability details improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains outweigh the abstract's less qualified 'in general' wording, while the central construction, theory, and empirical findings remain unchanged.
